import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/sleep_health.csv')

# Preprocessing: Fill NaN in 'Sleep Disorder' for better visualization
# Assuming NaN implies no sleep disorder for this context.
df['Sleep Disorder'] = df['Sleep Disorder'].fillna('None')

# Set a clean seaborn style
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="viridis")

# Create a scatter plot to visualize the relationship between Sleep Duration and Quality of Sleep,
# faceted by Sleep Disorder and colored by Stress Level.
# This allows us to see how these core sleep metrics vary under different conditions.
g = sns.relplot(
    data=df,
    x="Sleep Duration",
    y="Quality of Sleep",
    hue="Stress Level",  # Color points based on Stress Level (gradient)
    size="Physical Activity Level", # Size points based on Physical Activity Level
    col="Sleep Disorder", # Create separate subplots for each Sleep Disorder category
    kind="scatter",
    palette="magma", # A sequential palette for 'Stress Level' is suitable
    height=4.5,
    aspect=1.2,
    s=150, # Base size for markers
    alpha=0.7, # Transparency for overlapping points
    col_wrap=2, # Wrap columns after 2 subplots if there are many disorder types
    legend="full" # Show the full legend for hue and size
)

# Add a main title to the figure
g.fig.suptitle("Sleep Duration vs. Quality of Sleep by Stress Level, Physical Activity, and Sleep Disorder", y=1.05, fontsize=16)

# Set axis labels for clarity
g.set_axis_labels("Sleep Duration (hours)", "Quality of Sleep (1-10 scale)")

# Set titles for individual subplots (facets)
g.set_titles(col_template="{col_name}")

# Adjust layout to prevent labels from overlapping and ensure everything fits
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.03, 1, 0.98]) # Adjust rect to make space for the suptitle

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/sleep_health.csv')

# Preprocessing: Fill NaN in 'Sleep Disorder' for better visualization
# Assuming NaN implies no sleep disorder for this context.
df['Sleep Disorder'] = df['Sleep Disorder'].fillna('None')

# Set a clean seaborn style
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="viridis")

# Create a scatter plot to visualize the relationship between Sleep Duration and Quality of Sleep,
# faceted by Sleep Disorder and colored by Stress Level.
# This allows us to see how these core sleep metrics vary under different conditions.
g = sns.relplot(
    data=df,
    x="Sleep Duration",
    y="Quality of Sleep",
    hue="Stress Level",  # Color points based on Stress Level (gradient)
    size="Physical Activity Level", # Size points based on Physical Activity Level
    col="Sleep Disorder", # Create separate subplots for each Sleep Disorder category
    kind="scatter",
    palette="magma", # A sequential palette for 'Stress Level' is suitable
    height=4.5,
    aspect=1.2,
    s=150, # Base size for markers
    alpha=0.7, # Transparency for overlapping points
    col_wrap=2, # Wrap columns after 2 subplots if there are many disorder types
    legend="full" # Show the full legend for hue and size
)

# Add a main title to the figure
g.fig.suptitle("Sleep Duration vs. Quality of Sleep by Stress Level, Physical Activity, and Sleep Disorder", y=1.05, fontsize=16)

# Set axis labels for clarity
g.set_axis_labels("Sleep Duration (hours)", "Quality of Sleep (1-10 scale)")

# Set titles for individual subplots (facets)
g.set_titles(col_template="{col_name}")

# Adjust layout to prevent labels from overlapping and ensure everything fits
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.03, 1, 0.98]) # Adjust rect to make space for the suptitle
